before_results.readmission: The positive class is readmission within 30 days. A missed positive matters more because the patient may not be flagged for added discharge planning or follow-up; a false alarm may use resources for someone who would not be readmitted.
before_results.diabetes: The positive class is doctor diagnosis or HbA1c at least 6.5%. A missed positive matters more because the person may not be flagged for follow-up testing; a false alarm may lead to an unnecessary follow-up test.

recommendations.readmission: At 0.5, the models flag almost nobody. Random roest has the highest Test AUROC (0.651). At 0.10, its sensitivity is 54%, specificity 66%, precision 13.6%, and its flags 1,428 of 4,000 patients. You could choose "none is adequate" because it still misses about 46% of readmissions orchoose random forst at 0.10 while explicitly accepting the high false alarm workload.
recommendations.diabetes: If catching positive matters most, logistic regression at 0.10 is 1 option. Test AUROC 0.827, sensitivity 91%, specificity 52%, precision 30.7%, and 589 of 1052 patients flagged. At 0.2, its dlags fewer (390) and his higher precision (39.7%), but sensitivity falls to 78%. Therefore you should pick the balance you think is appropriate
